title: Systematic owns its defence and healthcare products, so its platform slot is filled by its own IP
content:
Systematic's tool field records no partner platform. It says the stack was not researched and notes instead that the firm owns defence and health products of its own. Its v2 verticals — defence, healthcare and public — are the markets those products serve.

For a mechanical rescore that reads size and slot occupancy, this is the awkward case. The platform slot is neither open nor occupied by a third-party vendor whose grip could be loosened; it is occupied by software the firm sells. Anything placed there would have to compete for room on its own product roadmap, which is a product-management decision, not a procurement one.

That is why the flag stops short of a verdict and asks for an OSS-portfolio screen first. A defence and public-sector product house is exactly the profile where the screen's answer changes the approach entirely: open-source components inside its own products would suggest one conversation, a wholly proprietary portfolio suggests none.
